like counts how often monk A named monk B as liked over three rounds, a binomial out of a constant 3 that no column holds, so it is filed count (eggprod ruling). McElreath's Statistical Rethinking 2022 course (week 8, recalled, not in the cache; the help page lists only the columns) fits a social relations model to Sampson's monks: like_AB and like_BA binomial with a generalized giving and receiving effect per monk and a correlated dyad pair; its priors were not read. The stack follows kl_dyads: each dyad's two directions become rows, the nominating monk (A, then B) and the nominated one swapping between them. lme4 syntax cannot correlate a monk's giving and receiving effects across the giver and receiver columns, so the two terms are independent here; the dyad pair is (1 | dyad_id) plus the observation-level dyad_id:direction term, exact for a non-negative correlation, and direction enters only that term (ignored). A_name and B_name label A and B; dislike, the second response, is row 2.

dislike, as like in row 1, is a binomial out of a constant 3 that no column holds, so it is filed count (eggprod ruling). The course's social relations model of the dislike nominations, the same stack and random structure as row 1, whose notes hold the rendering; like is the first response.

documented_prior: a ~ normal(0,1); Rho_gr ~ lkj_corr(4); sigma_gr ~ exponential(1); L_Rho_d ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(8); sigma_d ~ exponential(1)
notes: Statistical Rethinking (2nd ed.) R code 14.31, m14.7: giftsAB ~ poisson(lambdaAB) with log(lambdaAB) = a + gr[hidA,1] + gr[hidB,2] + d[did,1], and giftsBA likewise with hidA and hidB swapped and d[did,2], a social relations model over 25 households. The stack makes each dyad's two directions rows, the giving household (hidA, then hidB) and the receiving one swapping between them. lme4 syntax cannot correlate a household's giving and receiving effects (Rho_gr) across the giver and receiver columns, so the two terms are independent here. The dyad pair d[did, 1:2], equal sds and correlation Rho_d, is (1 | did) plus the observation-level did:direction term, exact for a non-negative correlation; direction enters only that term and is ignored. offset (relative rate of contact), drel1 to drel4, dlndist, dass and d0125 are unused by m14.7.

formula: read ~ factor(year) + rule2 + I(rule2 < 0) + factor(year):I(rule2 < 0) + (1 | rbd)
notes: ROS ChileSchools (Gelman, Hill and Vehtari 2020, ch. 21; Chay, McEwan and Urquiola 2005): chile_setup.R keeps the large urban schools (big == 1) and their complete cases, sets eligible = (rule2 < 0) for the P-900 program assigned by the 1988 scores, and renames cas92, cas88, mat92 and mat88 read92, read88, math92 and math88. chile_schools.Rmd fits the regression discontinuity stan_glm(read92 ~ eligible + rule2 + read88 + math88) and its variants, a model of the 1992 score given the 1988 ones, not of the occasions (published_model no). The Stata labels ('88 cas', '90 cas', '92 cas') date the measures, so the long form is school (rbd, one row each) x test year 88, 90 and 92, read and math named as the setup names them, ncas (labeled only '88 ncas') stacked beside them. The proposed model lets the eligible schools' reading score move apart from the others' after 1988, eligibility the recode I(rule2 < 0) in the formula only, with a random intercept per school. math is an alternate response, ncas unused; the x88 terms, the rule's constructs, the d-differences and regd1 to regd7 are derived. indice90 and indice92 lack an 88 occasion and stay outside the stack, unused, as do rgn88, region and cmb_regn (a country's regions), p90, big and the urban and rural codes.

ROS Congress (ch. 10 and 15): congress_setup.R builds one row per House district from the 1986, 1988 and 1990 election files in their common district order, with incumbency inc (-1 Republican incumbent, 0 open seat, 1 Democratic incumbent), the Democratic share of the two-party vote v and v_adj, uncontested races set to 0.25 and 0.75. congress.Rmd fits stan_glm(vote ~ past_vote + inc) of the 1988 adjusted share on the 1986 one and predicts 1990, a model of one occasion given the last (published_model no). The long form is district x election year, district numbering the rows, vote named as congress.Rmd names v88_adj and inc as it names inc88. The districts by year are a panel; the proposed model takes the year as a factor and a random intercept per district. v, the unadjusted share, is an alternate response.

formula: counts ~ year + sex + offset(log(ave(counts, year, FUN = sum))) + (1 + year | name_id)
notes: ROS Names (ch. 2): one row per name and sex, each year's births of the name from 1880 to 2010 in its own column. names.Rmd reads the cleaned copy allnames_clean.csv (excluded as its subset), takes 1931 to 2000, normalizes each year's counts by the year's total over all names, sets zero counts to 2 and fits lm(logcounts ~ I(years/10)) to each name's series and to windows of it, a separate trend per name. The long form is name x year, counts named as names.Rmd names the count matrix, name_id numbering the rows since a name repeats across sex. The random intercept and year slope per name are the reader's hierarchical extension of those per-name fits (published_model no, low, as ROS Storable), the year's total births the offset as names.Rmd normalizes by it. Most long rows are zero; a zero likely stands for fewer than five births, below the Social Security Administration's reporting threshold, as names.Rmd's replacement by 2 suggests. Unnamed: 0 is a row number. The long form runs to millions of rows.

formula: grade ~ period + school + sex + age + address + famsize + Pstatus + Medu + Fedu + traveltime + studytime + failures + schoolsup + famsup + paid + activities + nursery + higher + internet + romantic + famrel + freetime + goout + Dalc + Walc + health + absences + (1 | student)
notes: ROS Student (ch. 12; Cortez and Silva 2008, UCI): one row per student of the mathematics course, G1 and G2 the first and second period grades and G3 the final grade issued at the third period (student.txt), so the long form is student x period 1 to 3, grade the codebook's word, student numbering the rows. student.Rmd fits stan_glm(G3mat ~ .) on student-merged.csv, the students of both courses, with the predictors filed here and G3mat > 0, the final grade alone (published_model no). The proposed model keeps those predictors, adds the period and a random intercept per student. A zero grade marks a student who left, which the source's G3 > 0 subset drops. school (GP, MS) is a two-school design factor; Mjob, Fjob, reason and guardian, which ROS leaves out, are unused.

formula: grade ~ period + school + sex + age + address + famsize + Pstatus + Medu + Fedu + traveltime + studytime + failures + schoolsup + famsup + paid + activities + nursery + higher + internet + romantic + famrel + freetime + goout + Dalc + Walc + health + absences + (1 | student)
notes: As student-mat.csv, for the Portuguese language course: G1, G2 and G3 the three period grades (student.txt), the long form student x period 1 to 3, student numbering the rows. student.Rmd fits the final grade alone on student-merged.csv and says G3por would serve likewise (published_model no); the proposed model keeps ROS's predictors, adds the period and a random intercept per student. school is a two-school design factor; Mjob, Fjob, reason and guardian are unused.

Read Coop/riverbay.Rmd (ROS ch. 4) and rosdata's riverbay page: each candidate's (V1) cumulative votes in the Riverbay co-op board election at six points of the count, after 600, 1200, 2444, 3444, 4444 and 5553 voters (the Rmd's voters vector, the occasions here); V8 a pseudonym the Rmd prints for some candidates. Long form candidate x count round; V1 names each candidate once. The Rmd compares the spread of each candidate's share between rounds with its binomial expectation and fits no model, so the model is proposed: each candidate's share of the voters counted, the occasion entering as the trials as in the Rmd's proportions. The tallies are cumulative, so a round's count contains the earlier rounds'; the candidates are every candidate of one election, many enough for a panel.

conversation_python.ipynb (deposit kr9fb) z-scores the pooled status ratings of both waves (status_all), writes this file as status_all.pivot(index='sid', columns='rater', values='status') for the ICC, and fits smf.mixedlm('status ~ 1 + sid', status_all, groups=rater) for the paper's per-participant status (Methods: participant ID as predictor, random intercepts for raters). The stack restores status_all without speaker_id and group: 468 ratings of 39 participants by 16 raters, wave one's AW to KS and wave two's cg to tl; status_wave_two.csv holds wave two alone on the raw scale.

RULE GAP: incumbency_88 is the 1988 race's alone (+1 a Democratic incumbent running, 0 open, -1 a Republican one) and repeats to the 1986 rows, a measure absent at 1986. ARM Ch. 7 README: vote_86 and vote_88 are the Democratic share of the two-party vote in the 343 congressional districts contested in 1988; 7.3_SimulationForNonLinearPredictions.R builds them from cong3/<year>.asc, setting uncontested 1986 races to 0.25 or 0.75 (35 rows), and congress.stan fits lm(vote_88 ~ vote_86 + incumbency_88), one election on the other, not a model of the occasions, so published_model no. The long form is district x year; the model is proposed.

formula: cbind(r, n - r) ~ 0 + factor(trial) + arm + (0 + I(as.numeric(arm == 't')) | trial)
documented_prior: mu ~ normal(0, sqrt(1E5)); d ~ normal(0, 1E3); sigmasq_delta ~ inv_gamma(1E-3, 1E-3)
notes: blocker.stan (BUGS Vol1 Blockers, 22 trials) fits rt ~ binomial_logit(nt, mu + delta) and rc ~ binomial_logit(nc, mu): a baseline log-odds mu per trial under a vague normal(0, sqrt(1E5)) prior, a fixed trial effect, and a log odds ratio delta per trial ~ student_t(4, d, sigma_delta). The data dict's arm-level arrays set the stack: r events of n at the control (rc, nc) and treated (rt, nt) arm, the arm named by the columns' suffixes c and t since the code names neither, trial numbering the rows. Written as fixed trial intercepts and a random effect on the treated-arm indicator, filed as an uncorrelated arm slope (as metadat dat.tian2009); lme4's normal random effect only approximates the student_t(4), so confidence is medium. delta_new is a predictive draw.

documented_prior: mu ~ normal(0.0, 1000); phi ~ normal(0.0, 1000); pi ~ normal(0.0, 1000); sigmasq1 ~ inv_gamma(.001, .001); sigmasq2 ~ inv_gamma(.001, .001)
notes: equiv.stan (BUGS Vol1 Equiv, bioequivalence in a cross-over trial) fits Y[n, p] ~ normal(mu + sign[T[n, p]] * phi / 2 + sign[p] * pi / 2 + delta[n], sigma1) with delta ~ normal(0, sigma2), a random intercept per subject. The data dict's Y[N, P] sets the stack: period 1 and 2 from Y_1 and Y_2, subject numbering the 10 rows. T[n, p] = (group * (2 * p - 3) + 3) %/% 2 is the tablet taken in period p, so the treatment contrast sign[T] is group * (3 - 2 * period), an expression in the formula only, and sign[p] the period effect. group (1 or -1, the sequence) enters equiv.stan only through that contrast; covariates and interactions file it as group and group:period, which span the contrast and add a sequence effect equiv.stan leaves out. theta = exp(phi) and the equivalence indicator are generated quantities.

formula: cbind(r, n - r) ~ 0 + factor(study) + arm + (0 + I(as.numeric(arm == 't')) | study)
documented_prior: mu ~ uniform(-10, 10); pc ~ uniform(0, 1); tau under six priors: inv_tau_sq_1 ~ gamma(0.001, 0.001); tau_sq_2 ~ uniform(0, 50); tau_3 ~ uniform(0, 50); B0 ~ uniform(0, 1) with tau^2 = s0_sq * (1 - B0) / B0; D0 ~ uniform(0, 1) with tau = sqrt(s0_sq) * (1 - D0) / D0; tau_sq_6 ~ normal(0, p0_sigma) T[0, ], s0_sq = 0.1272041, p0_sigma = 1 / sqrt(Phi(0.75) / s0_sq)
notes: magnesium.stan (BUGS Vol1 Magnesium, 8 studies) fits rc ~ binomial(nc, pc) and rt ~ binomial_logit(nt, theta + logit(pc)): a control-arm probability pc per study under uniform(0, 1), a fixed study effect, and a log odds ratio theta per study ~ normal(mu, tau). The data dict's arm-level arrays set the stack: r events of n at the control (rc, nc) and treated (rt, nt) arm, the arm named by the columns' suffixes c and t, study numbering the rows. Written as fixed study intercepts and a random effect on the treated-arm indicator, filed as an uncorrelated arm slope (as metadat dat.tian2009). The file fits the one model under six priors on tau at once, a sensitivity analysis with a theta and pc per prior; OR = exp(mu) per prior is generated.

formula: cbind(r, n - r) ~ 0 + factor(stratum) + arm + arm:year + arm:I(year^2 - 22) + (0 + arm | stratum)
documented_prior: mu ~ normal(0, 1000); alpha ~ normal(0.0, 1000); beta1 ~ normal(0.0, 1000); beta2 ~ normal(0.0, 1000); sigma_sq ~ inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001)
notes: oxford.stan (WinBUGS Vol1 p. 34, Oxford: smooth fit to log-odds ratios) fits r0 ~ binomial_logit(n0, mu) and r1 ~ binomial_logit(n1, alpha + mu + beta1 * year + beta2 * (year^2 - 22) + b * sigma) with b ~ normal(0, 1): a log-odds mu per stratum under normal(0, 1000), a fixed stratum effect, and a log odds ratio of arm 1 against arm 0 per stratum, quadratic in year with a normal deviation of sd sigma. The data dict's arm-level arrays set the stack: r of n at arm 0 (r0, n0) and arm 1 (r1, n1), the arm valued by the columns' suffixes since the code names neither, stratum numbering the 120 rows. year (-10 to 10) is a stratum covariate that enters only through arm; its square is filed once as year.

formula: log(t) ~ MWG + NWG + KWG + MDIMC + NDIMC + MDIMA + NDIMB + KWI + VWM + VWN + STRM + STRN + SA + SB + (1 | z0)
notes: UCI readme: 241,600 feasible parameter combinations of the SGEMM GPU kernel, each run four times (Run1 (ms) to Run4 (ms)), the log run time advised. LMMNN's r_scripts/lme4_on_datasets/lme4_sgemm.R (read in registry/help/_pass162/readers/ml/lmmnn) numbers the combinations z0, pivot_longer()s the four runs into t, drops run_id and fits lmer(log(t) ~ the 14 parameters + (1 | z0)) in 5-fold cross-validation; the stack numbers z0 from 1 where the script counts from 0. The ten tiling and width parameters are numeric as LMMNN reads them, STRM, STRN, SA and SB binary.

formula: meanIBI ~ Time * Condition + Age + Gender + Alcohol + Caffeine + Eat + (1 | SubID)
notes: RULE GAP: the script's covariate BMI.c centers a BMI column the deposited table lacks, and Height is free text in mixed units (63, 5'2, 152), so BMI is left out of the formula. 2.1 Analyses_SciReports_revision.R keeps the participants with cardiovascular data, pivots the baseline., stress. and recovery. columns of meanIBI, logRSA and CSI by Time (stress renamed DST), the stack filed here with meanHR and logHRV, and fits IBI_2 = lmer(meanIBI ~ Time*Condition + BMI.c + Age.c + Gender.recode + Alcohol + Caffeine + Eat + (1|SubID)), filed here: Age.c is Age mean-centered, and Gender.recode relabels the codes 1, 2 and 3 after four hand fixes, where the file's Gender also holds 8, 1,9 and 2,7. formula: CSI ~ Time * Condition + Age + Gender + Alcohol + Caffeine + Eat + (1 | SubID)
